why: 3.0 has a decimal point, so Python treats it as a float.

q: Which symbol starts a single-line comment in Python?
why: Python uses # for comments; everything after it on the line is ignored.
// is floor division: 7 divided by 2 is 3.5, floored to 3.
Multiplying a string by an integer repeats it.

q: Which is a valid variable name in Python?
why: Names can't start with a digit, can't contain '-', and can't be a keyword like class.
Index -1 means the last item of the list.
Functions are created with def.
% is the remainder operator: 10 ÷ 3 leaves remainder 1.
Assigning a new key adds it, so the dictionary ends with 3 items.

code: print([x * x for x in range(4)])
why: range(4) gives 0..3 and each value is squared.
Slices include the start index and exclude the end index: characters 1, 2, 3.
An empty list is falsy, so bool([]) is False.
y uses its default value 2, so f(3) returns 3 * 2.
Tuples are immutable, so item assignment raises TypeError.
sorted() returns a new sorted list of the characters.
list() forces the map to produce values; each element gets +1.

code:
def add(x, lst=[]):
    lst.append(x)
    return lst

print(add(1))
print(add(2))
why: The default list is created once when the function is defined and shared between calls — a classic gotcha.

code:
gen = (x for x in range(3))
print(list(gen))
print(list(gen))
why: A generator can be consumed only once; the second list() finds it exhausted.

code:
fs = [lambda: i for i in range(3)]
print([f() for f in fs])
why: The lambdas look up i when called, after the loop finished (i == 2). This is late binding.
Floating-point numbers can't represent 0.1 and 0.2 exactly; the sum is 0.30000000000000004.
copy() is shallow: the inner lists are shared, so appending through b changes a too.
* unpacks the list into separate arguments; sep controls what goes between them.
bool is a subclass of int in Python, so True is an instance of int.

q: What is the average time complexity of checking `x in my_set` for a Python set?
why: Sets are hash tables, so membership tests take constant time on average.

title: Sum of a list
statement: Return the sum of all the numbers in the list. An empty list should return 0.
hint: Start with a total of 0 and add each number to it in a loop.

title: Even or odd
statement: Return true if the number is even, otherwise false.
hint: A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is 0.

title: Reverse a string
hint: Python slices with [::-1]. In JavaScript: split into characters, reverse, join.

title: Count the vowels
statement: Return how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u — upper or lower case) are in the text.
hint: Convert to lower case first so you only check five letters.
solution:
def count_vowels(s):
    return sum(1 for ch in s.lower() if ch in "aeiou")

title: Palindrome check
statement: Return true if the text reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring upper/lower case and any character that is not a letter or digit.

examples.call: is_palindrome("A man, a plan, a canal: Panama")

hint: Build a cleaned version containing only letters and digits in lower case, then compare it with its reverse.
tests: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

title: FizzBuzz
statement: Return a list of strings for 1..n: "Fizz" for multiples of 3, "Buzz" for multiples of 5, "FizzBuzz" for both, otherwise the number as a string.
hint: Check the multiple-of-15 case first, otherwise it will be caught by the Fizz or Buzz branch.

title: Two Sum
statement: Given a list of numbers and a target, return the two indexes [i, j] (with i < j) whose values add up to the target. Exactly one solution exists.
hint: Store each number's index in a dictionary/Map as you go, and look up target - current before storing.

title: Group the anagrams
statement: Group words that are anagrams of each other. Return a list of groups; sort the words inside each group alphabetically, and sort the groups by their first word.
hint: Two words are anagrams when their sorted letters are identical — use the sorted letters as a dictionary key.

title: Longest substring without repeats
statement: Return the length of the longest substring that contains no repeated character.
hint: Slide a window: remember the last index of each character, and move the window start just past a repeat.
